extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of electric generating units (EGUs), environmental compliance officers, permitting authorities, and EGU monitoring/engineering staff
extracted.subtask_short: GHG standards for electric generating units
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements in EPA 40 CFR Part 60, Subpart TTTT: applicability, CO2 emission standards, monitoring/measurement, compliance calculations, reporting, and CO2 capture/waiver procedures for affected steam generating units, IGCCs, and stationary combustion turbines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of subpart (affected EGU definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart establishes emission standards and compliance schedules for GHG emissions from steam generating units, IGCC facilities, and stationary combustion turbines that commence construction, reconstruction, or modification within specified date ranges; affected units are referred to as affected electric generating units (EGUs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to units that commence construction after Jan 8, 2014, commence reconstruction after June 18, 2014, or commence modification after Jan 8, 2014, but on or before May 23, 2023 (dates differ slightly by unit type). An affected EGU for applicability purposes is a steam generating unit, IGCC, or stationary combustion turbine as defined in the subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability thresholds (size and electricity sales)
rubrics_metrics.description: The GHG standards apply only to units that (1) have a base load rating greater than 260 GJ/h (250 MMBtu/h) of fossil fuel and (2) serve a generator or generators capable of selling greater than 25 MW of electricity to a utility distribution system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both conditions (base load rating and generator capacity to sell >25 MW) must be met for applicability except where other specific exceptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions and exceptions to applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: You are not subject to the subpart if your EGU meets any of the listed exceptions (paragraphs (b)(1) through (10)), including limited net-electric sales, high non-fossil fuel fraction with permitted capacity factor limit, certain combined heat and power restrictions, small effective generation capacity, certain waste combustors/incinerators, minor modifications with ≤10% CO2 hourly increase, turbines not capable of burning natural gas, >50% industrial-process-derived heat input with no external useful output, or being subject to subpart TTTTa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each exemption has specific conditions (for example, paragraph (b)(1) requires a federally enforceable permit limiting annual net-electric sales to ≤ one-third of potential output or 219,000 MWh). Carefully confirm permit conditions, capacity calculations, and whether the modification increase is ≤10% (two significant figures) when claiming exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to meet CO2 emissions standard (tables 1 or 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must not discharge gases containing CO2 in excess of the applicable CO2 emission standard specified in table 1 or 2 to this subpart, consistent with paragraphs (b), (c), and (d) of §60.5520.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance must be determined consistent with the selected basis (gross or net energy output or heat-input-based) and related monitoring/recordkeeping/reporting methodologies included in the operating permit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross versus net energy output standard and permit inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as specified, you must comply with the applicable gross or net energy output standard; your operating permit must include monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting methodologies based on the chosen gross or net energy output standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For most sources the term 'gross energy output' applies; stationary combustion turbine owners/operators may petition to comply with net energy output standard per §60.5520(c). Operating permits must reflect the selected basis and methodologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to use net energy output for stationary combustion turbines
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner/operator of a stationary combustion turbine may petition the Administrator in writing to comply with the alternate applicable net energy output standard; if granted, the turbine must comply with the net output standard and the operating permit must include monitoring/recordkeeping/reporting based on net output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators who elect net must petition to switch back to gross output if desired. The petition must be written to the Administrator and compliance begins on the date the Administrator grants the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform fuel monitoring exemption for stationary combustion turbines
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of stationary combustion turbines permitted to burn only 'uniform fuels' that result in a consistent emission rate of ≤69 kg/GJ (160 lb/MMBtu) are not subject to monitoring or reporting requirements under this subpart and are only required to maintain purchase records for permitted fuels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform fuels include hydrogen, natural gas, methane, butane, ethane, propane, naphtha, jet fuel kerosene, No. 1 and No. 2 fuel oil, biodiesel, etc. This exemption applies only if permitted fuels meet the consistent emission rate requirement and fuel purchase records are maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-uniform fuel monitoring requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of stationary combustion turbines permitted to burn non-uniform fuels or fuels that exceed the uniform fuel emission rate must follow the monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements necessary to complete heat input-based calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-uniform fuels (e.g., residual oil, non-jet kerosene) require monitoring sufficient to determine heat input and CO2 emissions according to the methods specified in the subpart and in 40 CFR part 75.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance determination frequency and averaging period
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with the applicable CO2 emission standard shall be determined on a 12-operating-month rolling average basis; you must determine compliance monthly by calculating the average CO2 emissions rate at the end of each 12-operating-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initial compliance determination is made within 30 days after the end of the initial 12-operating-month compliance period. Detailed rules determine the first month of the initial compliance period depending on commercial operation dates and reporting triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heat-input-based standard calculation for mixed fuels (Equation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If subject to an input-based standard, you must determine the applicable emissions standard during the compliance period using the weighted equation based on heat input from natural gas (HTIP_ng) and heat input from other fuels (HTIP_o) with allowable rates of 50 kg/GJ for natural gas and 69 kg/GJ for other fuels (use lb/MMBtu equivalents if electing lb units).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use one of the methods in §60.5535(d)(2) to determine heat inputs; plug values into the provided equation and use the specified constants (50 and 69 kg/GJ) or corresponding lb/MMBtu values (120 and 160).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operate and maintain consistent with safety and good air pollution control practice
rubrics_metrics.description: At all times you must operate and maintain each affected EGU, including associated equipment and monitors, in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrator will determine if operations and maintenance are consistent based on fuel use records, monitoring results, O&M procedures and records, subpart reports, and inspections. Maintain documentation to demonstrate good practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial compliance determination timing and first operating month rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days after the end of the initial compliance period you must make an initial compliance determination; rules define the first month of the initial 12-operating-month period based on commercial operation date and whether the unit is subject to Acid Rain program reporting triggers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different subclauses specify how to pick the first operating month for units commencing commercial operation on/after Oct 23, 2015, units comm. op. before that date, and modified/reconstructed EGUs that become subject to the subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring plan preparation and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: For affected sources (except turbines qualifying under §60.5520(d)(1)), you must prepare a monitoring plan to quantify hourly CO2 mass emissions (tons/h) in accordance with 40 CFR 75.53(g) and (h); the electronic portion must be submitted using the ECMPS Client Tool and must be in place prior to reporting emissions data or monitoring system certification test results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring plans must be updated as necessary and submittals must be made by the Designated Representative (DR), Alternate DR, or delegated agent per §60.5555(d) and (e).

rubrics_metrics.name: CO2 continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For affected EGUs that combust coal you must install (and for others you may install) a CO2 CEMS to directly measure hourly average CO2 concentrations and a flow monitoring system to measure hourly average stack gas flow rates per 40 CFR 75.10(a)(3)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an alternative to CO2 concentration measurement (if not using carbon capture), you may use a certified O2 monitor to calculate CO2 concentrations per 40 CFR 75.10(a)(3)(iii). If CO2 is measured on a dry basis, you must also install and operate a continuous moisture monitoring system per 40 CFR 75.11(b) or use fuel-specific default moisture values or petition for site-specific default under 40 CFR 75.66.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification and quality assurance for continuous monitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Each continuous monitoring system used to determine CO2 mass emissions must meet the applicable certification and quality assurance procedures in 40 CFR 75.20 and appendices A and B to 40 CFR part 75.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the referenced part 75 certification and QA procedures for system certification, QA/QC, and ongoing quality checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of unadjusted exhaust gas volumetric flow rates
rubrics_metrics.description: You must use only unadjusted exhaust gas volumetric flow rates to determine hourly CO2 mass emissions; you must not apply the bias adjustment factors described in Section 7.6.5 of appendix A to 40 CFR part 75 to flow rate data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure flow data used in calculations are the raw volumetric flow rates without applying the specified bias adjustments from appendix A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow monitor setup and RATA reference method and pitot tube calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: You must select an appropriate reference method to set up (characterize) the flow monitor and perform RATAs, in accordance with 40 CFR part 75. If using a Type-S pitot tube or pitot assembly for flow RATAs you must calibrate it and you may not use the 0.84 default Type-S pitot coefficient specified in Method 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow part 75 reference methods for flow monitor characterization and RATA procedures; calibrate pitot tubes and do not rely on default coefficients where prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hourly CO2 mass emissions calculation and valid operating hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate hourly CO2 mass emissions (kg) according to the referenced equations/procedures (appendix F to part 75) and perform calculations only for 'valid operating hours' as defined in §60.5540(a)(1). Convert tons to kg by multiplying by 907.2 and round per specified rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with tons/h from equation F-11 or appendix F methods depending on wet/dry measurement, multiply by operating time to get tons, convert to kg (×907.2), and round to nearest kg (or two significant figures where specified). Record hourly values and operating times as required under 40 CFR 75.57(e) and report under 40 CFR 75.64(a)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Output-based measurement instrumentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If subject to an output-based emissions standard you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate sufficient watt meters to continuously measure and record hourly gross or net electric output using 0.2 class electricity metering instrumentation and ANSI C12.20-2010 calibration procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For CHP EGUs, also install meters to continuously determine and record total useful thermal output hour-by-hour. For process steam, install/operate meters to continuously determine hourly steam flow rate, temperature, and pressure. The monitoring plan must ensure hour-by-hour recording of each component used in the determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportioning combined gross/net energy output for multiple EGUs serving a common generator
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more affected EGUs serve a common electric generator, apportion combined hourly gross or net energy output to individual EGUs according to fraction of total steam load and/or direct mechanical energy contributed by each EGU; alternatively, if EGUs are identical, apportion by fraction of heat input contributed by each EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may elect to develop and demonstrate alternate apportionment methods satisfactory to the Administrator; Administrator may approve alternate methods if they ensure accurate estimation of regulated emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring options for EGUs sharing a common exhaust stack
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more affected EGUs that implement the continuous emission monitoring provisions share a common exhaust stack, you must monitor hourly CO2 mass emissions using one of the procedures: (1) monitor at the common stack if EGUs share the same emissions standard and use sum of hourly loads (stack operating hours), or (2) monitor each EGU separately prior to mixing, or apportion CO2 emissions based on unit load contribution and F-factors if EGUs are subject to different standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If monitoring at common stack and compliance attained, each EGU sharing the stack is in compliance. Alternate apportionment methods may be proposed for Administrator approval if they ensure accurate estimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and requirements for valid operating hours/data
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'valid operating hour' is an operating hour for which valid data are obtained for all parameters used to determine hourly CO2 mass emissions and, if a heat-input-based standard applies, for all parameters used to determine total heat input; corresponding hourly gross/net energy output must also be valid data (zero counts as valid for hours with no useful output).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must exclude hours where substitute data provisions of part 75 are applied for parameters used, exceedances of full-scale range of CEMS occur for parameters used, or total gross/net energy output or total heat input is unavailable. These rules determine which hours count toward the compliance calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum valid operating hours fraction (95% rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each 12-operating-month compliance period, at least 95 percent of the operating hours in the compliance period must be valid operating hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fewer than 95% of hours are valid in the compliance period, follow applicable remedial/reporting rules; ensure monitoring systems and data completeness to meet this performance metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summation of valid hourly CO2 mass emissions for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: For each compliance period, total CO2 mass emissions must be calculated by summing the valid hourly CO2 mass emissions values for all valid operating hours in the period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hourly CO2 mass emissions calculated under §60.5535(b) or (c) as applicable; ensure proper inclusion/exclusion per valid hour rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of hourly gross/net energy output (P_gross/net) and its components
rubrics_metrics.description: For each valid operating hour used in the compliance calculation, determine the corresponding hourly gross or net energy output (P_gross/net) in MWh per the specified equation (components include electric/mechanical output from steam turbines, stationary combustion turbines, integrated equipment, feedwater pump energy, auxiliary loads, useful thermal outputs, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert reported hourly gross or net energy outputs to MWh by multiplying by operating time. Use provided component definitions and the Transmission and Distribution Factor (TDF) value (0.95 for certain CHP EGUs meeting thresholds, otherwise 1.0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of useful thermal output (P_tPS) for CHP/processes
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, calculate useful thermal output (P_tPS) using measured thermal output flow (Qm), enthalpy (H), and conversion factor CF (3.6×10^9 J/MWh or 3.413×10^6 Btu/MWh) per the provided equation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure thermal flow and enthalpy at the measured temperature and pressure (or energy in condensate return line where applicable); convert to MWh using CF to include thermal output in denominator for emission rate calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis calculation for 12-operating-month emission rate (output vs heat-input basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources complying with energy output-based standards must calculate the denominator by summing hourly gross/net energy outputs for valid hours; sources complying with heat-input-based standards must calculate total heat input for each fuel fired for the compliance period, including all valid operating hours and following fuel-specific monitoring procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure fuel-specific procedures under the selected monitoring option (§60.5535(d)(2)) are followed when calculating total heat input; separately compute denominators depending on standard type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation and rounding of CO2 mass emissions rate
rubrics_metrics.description: For output-based standards calculate the CO2 mass emissions rate (kg/MWh) by dividing total CO2 mass emissions by total gross/net energy output; for heat-input-based standards calculate (kg/GJ or lb/MMBtu) by dividing total CO2 mass emissions by total heat input. Round results to two significant figures if <1000, three significant figures if >1000 (or two sig figs for heat-input-based results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the specified rounding conventions for reporting and compliance determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements for compliance submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports must include, among other things, the percentage of valid operating hours in each 12-operating-month compliance period and the CO2 emissions standard (as identified in table 1 or 2) with which the affected EGU must comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the detailed reporting schedule and content in §60.5555 and related sections; ensure inclusion of required metrics and identification of applicable standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: CO2 capture reporting pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: If your affected EGU captures CO2 to meet the applicable emissions standard you must report in accordance with 40 CFR part 98, subpart PP, and either: (1) report per part 98 subpart RR or VV if injection occurs on-site; (2) transfer captured CO2 to an EGU/facility that reports under part 98 subpart RR or VV if injection occurs off-site; or (3) transfer captured CO2 to a facility with an innovative technology waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure captured CO2 handling and reporting comply with the selected subpart; maintain records and transfer documentation as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver process and criteria for non-RR/VV transfer destination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may request an Administrator waiver of the requirement that captured CO2 be transferred to a facility reporting under part 98 subpart RR or VV. To receive a waiver the applicant must demonstrate the technology will store captured CO2 as effectively as geologic sequestration and will not cause or contribute to unreasonable risk to public health, welfare, or safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrator considers factors such as operating history, whether the technology increases emissions/releases of other pollutants, and permanence of storage. Administrator may require tests, grant conditional approval with monitoring/reporting conditions, and withdraw approval on evidence of releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference of external technical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Various external standards (ANSI, ASME, ASTM, ISO, CSA, EN, etc.) are incorporated by reference for specific measurement, metering, testing, and performance requirements throughout the subpart (e.g., ANSI C12.20-2010 for 0.2 class electricity metering instrumentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the listed incorporated documents (and their approved versions/dates) for the detailed technical requirements they impose; references include contact info and the IBR-approved sections in which they apply (see §60.17 and the referenced list).
